turn_text: And readership in readership success rates amongst the lower grade students is experiencing some trouble here in the area. How does that rank on your list of priorities here? It sounds like you have been engaging with some students. What more are you doing for those types of struggling students, struggling school systems for those types of reading rates?

Well, that's always handled at the local level. I mean, every school district in America has their own standards and all of that. At the federal level, we are less about having policy as far as the curriculum, more about the funding from that angle. So that's a local programming type of thing. But I do something else. I talk a lot about reading in communities. I go to all over our congressional district where there's something that we have that we call the Library of Congress book program. And the Library of Congress has surplus books. They have more books than they have shelf space for. So as a member of Congress, I'm allowed to go over to the Library of Congress and pick out the books that are in their surplus box. It's like, you know, literally they have a room full of all these books. and we can take whatever we want as long as we give them to non-profits. That's the only criteria. So I have chosen small town libraries all over our congressional district to donate those two and we've gone to, we've been doing this for about five years now and every time I go again I talk about the importance of reading and you know as a kid growing up probably what I loved more than anything else were number one playing sports and number two reading. I've just always loved to read and could just totally get lost in a book. So, you know, I talk to the kids about my own love of reading and, you know, love going to these libraries and these small towns all over the congressional district.
